Risk-aware DRL methods now incorporate volatility, drawdown, and tail risk constraints directly into the reward or optimization objective, while multiobjective frameworks enable fine-grained control of risk/return trade-offs across diverse investors [Lwele et al., 2025, Deng et al., 2024]. In options and volatility trading, multi-agent architectures that separate the decision to take risk from the policy used to hedge it have been shown to improve risk-adjusted performance relative to traditional or single-agent baselines [Bańka and Chudziak, 2025, Chen et al., 2025]. At the same time, explainable AI (XAI) techniques and sentimentaware tail risk models demonstrate that interpretable drivers of risk can be extracted and communicated to portfolio managers and risk committees [Exp, 2023, Klinkert, 2024]. This paper surveys these developments and proposes a research agenda for autonomous portfolio and derivatives risk management agents that (i) monitor Greeks, volatility regime shifts, and liquidity, (ii) dynamically hedge multi-asset portfolios, and (iii) use scenario-simulation agents t…
